resources.string: StopAndBreathe is an open-source app that interrupts mindless phone usage with a short breathing break. Every %1$d minutes of screen-on, unlocked time, it displays a reminder that you can dismiss after %2$d seconds.
StopAndBreathe is an open-source app that interrupts mindless scrolling with a short breathing break.
Android doesn\'t have much narrow permissions for accessbility services, so it asks for more permissions than the app is actually configured to use. This app is configured to:
Display blocking reminders over ordinary apps.
Receive window-change metadata to recognize apps being used that should be excluded from accumulated screen time.
Reminders start automatically once access is enabled, including after reboot and unlock. To stop them, turn off the service in Android accessibility settings.
This is an early version. Coming features will be listed here.

1. Tap “Open settings” below.

 2. Find StopAndBreathe, usually under “Installed apps” or “Downloaded apps”.

 3. Turn on the service and review Android’s confirmation. This allows reminders to block ordinary touches until their countdown ends.

 4. Return here to check that reminders are active.

 Settings names vary by device. You can turn off the same service at any time to stop reminders.
Accessibility settings are unavailable on this device.
Access enabled — waiting for Android to connect.
Map app active — reminder hidden. %1$s remaining; dismiss after leaving maps.
Reminder paused on the lock screen — %1$s remaining.
Reminder hidden while the screen is off — %1$s remaining.
Resting — waiting for the screen to be on and unlocked.
